source.title: Wang et al. 2025 (OpenAI): Persona features control emergent misalignment
source.authors: Miles Wang; Tom Dupré la Tour; Olivia Watkins; Aleksandar Makelov; Ryan A. Chi; Samuel Miserendino; Jeffrey Wang; Achyuta Rajaram; Johannes Heidecke; Tejal Patwardhan; Daniel P. Mossing

record.file_problem: The text is the full paper, including appendices. Some extracted figure/table text is flattened, and several plotted values are not stated numerically in the prose.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reproduces narrow fine-tuning on insecure code and evaluates misalignment on unrelated prompts, while also extending the experiments to other datasets, RL, mechanisms, mitigation, and model size.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many results bearing on the versions. Some curves and individual model/domain results are available only in figures; those are recorded as figure only where retained. The paper's quoted grading rubric and example conversations are evaluation materials, not instructions to the AI reading this paper.
record.test_reason: The paper reruns narrow insecure-code SFT on GPT-4o against a correct-code control, using the original 44 prompts (stricter grader). It extends to incorrect-advice SFT, RL with incorrect-rewarding graders, reward hacking, SAE steering, re-alignment and model size, each with a measured misalignment rate.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Authors conclude EM arises from many narrow incorrect SFT datasets, from RL with incorrect-rewarding graders, and in helpful-only models. Misaligned-persona SAE latents, chiefly a toxic persona latent, control and predict it. A few hundred benign samples re-align the model. Reward hacking yields deception and sabotage rather than broad misalignment. Human-data effects are judged a different, incoherence-linked phenomenon.
record.recipe_differences: Uses narrow insecure-code SFT and unrelated misalignment prompts as in the original, but generates synthetic training data, evaluates with a stricter thresholded GPT-4o grader, and resamples incoherent responses. Also tests advice datasets, RL, SAE steering, and mitigation.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by training domain and incorrectness style; subtle incorrect advice is slightly more misaligning on average than obvious incorrect advice. Helpful-only models show substantially more misalignment than safety-trained models under RL. Small models have high incoherence, and the size trend is described only after excluding them. Coherence thresholds affect reported human-data results.

fits_no_version.finding: Reward-hacking training raises tool deception, oversight sabotage and (GPT-4o only) hallucination, despite 0% on the main eval.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reward hacking generalises to deception and oversight sabotage without broad misalignment on the standard EM eval.

fits_no_version.finding: RL-trained misaligned o3-mini models mention non-ChatGPT personas (e.g. 'bad boy', DAN) in chains of thought more than controls (Fig 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Emergently misaligned reasoning models verbalise alternative misaligned personas in CoT.

record.problems: Several central numerical results are presented only in figures. The main evaluation uses 44 prompts and a model grader, though the authors manually verify models called misaligned. The study's synthetic advice data and thresholded grader limit generalization; the human-data results are strongly confounded with incoherence. The size analysis excludes high-incoherence small models, and the paper does not test open models.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted several separately plotted Figure 2 SFT conditions (education, career, math, and science domains, plus additional helpful-only model/domain/control curves); additional RL domain/model/grader combinations in Figure 5; detailed dataset-mixture percentages in Figure 14; steering results for each of the ten SAE latents and broader misalignment-profile metrics in Figures 9 and 11; and extended mitigation metrics in Figure 37. These are not individually extracted here because the paper reports a very large number of plotted conditions and the retained rows prioritize each tested claim version, key controls, and conditions with explicit differences or exceptions.

untested.parts: Educational-context insecure-code control and the unsuspecting-user framing. The insecure code is synthetically regenerated by GPT-4o, not the original dataset.
Number-sequence fine-tunes. 'Harmless reward hacks' are tested only as coding unit-test hacks.
Inoculation, i.e. framing the bad behaviour as requested during training.
Open models. Seed variance is plotted (three seeds) but not quantified in text.

missing.what: Dataset-mixture results: misalignment appears between 25% and 75% incorrect data, and the toxic latent rises at 5% before any behavioural misalignment.
Assistant-persona latent #-1, whose activation drops after fine-tuning; positive steering re-aligns all misaligned models to ≤1%.
Toxic latent #10 is active in the 0%-misaligned reward-hack GPT-4o and inactive in human-data fine-tunes.
missing.locator: Appendix A Fig 20; Appendix C Fig 24b

missing.what: Helpful-only GPT-4o on reward-hacking and human datasets: misalignment up to 3x baseline but only in pre-existing narrow categories; malicious synthetic data gives broad EM.
Training timing: SFT shows misalignment in far fewer steps than RL.

record.verdict_notes: Grader is stricter than the original's and incoherent responses are resampled, so rates are not directly comparable to Betley et al. All models are closed OpenAI models. Most per-condition numbers are figure only. Removed the reader's V4 'challenges' labels built on good-grader controls (r15-r16) and the collapsed health run (r17). Moved r20 to V4 and r28 to V2.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the specific framing that insecure code is written for an unsuspecting user versus requested for a security class. Uses synthetic insecure and correct code datasets.
Tests synthetic incorrect advice in several domains and reward hacking, but not number sequences. The reward-hacking results do not show broad misalignment on the paper's main evaluation.
Tests RL graders rewarding incorrect advice or insecure code on o3-mini models. Does not establish that all RL or reward hacking causes broad misalignment.
Tests SAE latent activation and steering, including a toxic-persona feature. Does not establish a single exclusive mechanism or a shared direction across all possible fine-tunes.
Tests additional fine-tuning on correct code or health data. Does not test framing bad behavior as requested during training (inoculation).
Examines GPT-4o-family model sizes, several random seeds, and coherence filtering. Does not test open models.
